RPGME TEST RUN, 18 NOVEMBER 2026

Four buyers, four games,
seventeen rough spots

We played four made-up buyers through the live wizard on www.rpgme.ai and wrote down every place where the chat got in their way. Each slide shows one problem with the screenshot of the moment it happened.

WHAT HAPPENED AFTER BUILD IT!

A billing hold cost every game an hour, and the family game then failed a check

All four builds stopped at 80% at about 6:45 PM, because the image provider stopped answering and the system read that as a billing problem. It waited an hour by design and tried again at 7:45 PM. Three games then finished. The family game failed a check that compares the game's structure with the approved template, rebuilt once, failed again, and waits until 9:16 PM for its next try.

WHAT WE FOUND

Seventeen problems in four groups, from things that break to small polish

Every picture in this deck is a real screenshot from the run, with the problem lit up. Two cards rebuild text that came and went between screenshots, and they say so.

BROKEN

6
  • The partner's look fails
  • The placeholder is a dragon
  • Kid photos are ignored
  • The build stops once
  • System text leaks into the chat
  • The buyer becomes a friend extra

WRONG WORDS

4
  • Best friends get a first date question
  • No Graduation button
  • A lock-in line under the wrong person
  • Every pet is furry

EXTRA STEPS

3
  • Clear answers need a second tap
  • The friend's job is asked twice
  • Photo uploads get no reply

SMALLER

4
  • About 8 seconds per reply
  • The look ignores later answers
  • No time estimate on the build screen
  • A reaction garbles the joke
BROKENGay couple game, turn 41. Also the mixed couple and best friends.

The partner's look failed in three of the four games

Late in the interview, the chat said that the partner's looks hit a snag and that it would use a placeholder for now. That happened to Theo, Mina and Hannah. There was no retry button, and nothing later said whether the real look ever came.

A better way: show a Try again button right there, and tell the buyer before Build It! whether the real look is ready.

BROKENGay and mixed couple games, the finished games

And the placeholder turned the partner into a dragon

When a partner's look never arrives, the game builder swaps in the stock art of Elliot, the game's red house dragon. Theo and Mina both got the same dragon, so Theo talks to Ryan as a dragon.

The box art copies each character's picture, so a dragon with a sword stands in front of both boxes. Hannah's real look arrived in time, so her game is fine.

A better way: never publish a partner with stock art. Hold the build until the real look is ready, or ask the buyer to pick a look.

Where it happens: generator/gameTypes/anniversary/resolveCharacterAssets.ts, the "optional-art-unavailable" fallback to Elliot.

BROKENFamily game, turns 49 to 54

The kids' photos were uploaded, then never used

Rafael uploaded a photo of Mateo and a photo of Luna. Two questions later, a small line under a different question said that Mateo keeps the default look. The same line then came for Luna.

Behind the scenes, the service that makes the characters returned errors in three of the four games.

A better way: retry the kid's look by itself. If it still fails, say so in the chat with a button to try again or to pick a look by hand.

BROKENBest friends game, on a phone, after Build It!

The best-friends build stopped once after Build It!

Grace tapped Build It! and watched the progress screen. Then the screen changed to an error: Grace's own custom look was not ready yet. The Try again button worked, and the build went on.

The error screen came and went between two of our screenshots, so the card on the right rebuilds it from the page text, word for word.

A better way: retry the look by itself before the build starts, so the buyer never sees this stop.

BROKENBest friends game, turn 53, after Try again

System text showed up in the chat after Try again

When the chat came back, it held two messages meant for the system, not for the buyer. One was titled Portrait confirmation fingerprint (not a story fact) and held a 64-character code. The other was titled Confirmed appearance for the story.

These lines were just above the visible part of the screenshot, so the card rebuilds them from the page text.

A better way: keep system messages out of the chat history that the buyer sees.

BROKENBest friends game, turns 40 to 53

The buyer became a friend extra in her own game

When the wizard asked who Hannah's best friend is, Grace answered that it is her, Grace. The wizard then treated Grace as a separate friend. It asked what Grace does for work, and after Try again it showed the line What's your friend's name? Grace.

A better way: when the best friend is the buyer, skip the friend questions, or ask them as questions about the buyer.

WRONG WORDSBest friends game, turn 24

A best-friends game asks about a first date

Grace and Hannah are best friends, and the game is for a graduation. The wizard still asked where they went on their first date. Grace had to explain that it was not a date, and that their first hangout was the dorm kitchen at 2 a.m.

A better way: word the question by relationship. Friends get "first hangout", and couples get "first date".

WRONG WORDSBest friends game, turn 13

Graduation is not one of the occasion buttons

The only buttons were Birthday, Christmas and Just because. Grace typed "Her graduation from nursing school!" and the reply was only "Noted!". She could not tell whether the game would use it.

A better way: add Graduation and the other common occasions, and repeat a typed occasion back so the buyer knows it landed.

WRONG WORDSFamily game, turn 21

A line about Rafael's look sits under Camila's pictures

"That neat beard and gold chain? Perfection. Locked in!" is about Rafael's own look, which he picked one step earlier. It shows up right after Camila's look grid, and it names no one, so it reads as if it is about Camila.

A better way: put the person's name in the line, and show it right under the grid that it belongs to.

WRONG WORDSMixed couple game, turn 26. Also best friends and gay couple.

Every pet is "furry", even a parrot and a lizard

The wizard says "furry companion" as soon as the buyer says yes to a pet, before it knows what the animal is. Kiwi is a parrot, and Sir Reginald is a bearded dragon. Later, it also calls each pet "they" after the buyer said "he" or "she".

A better way: wait for the animal before the warm reply, or use a word that fits any pet, and keep the pronoun the buyer used.

EXTRA STEPSFamily game, turn 39. Best friends, turns 16 and 44.

Clear answers needed a second tap

Rafael's inside joke was plain: when someone burns the toast, the family yells "Chef Biscuit strikes again!". The wizard said it was not sure how to use that message and asked him to confirm it.

Hannah's favorite movie, Mamma Mia!, was flagged as a song. Grace's answer about her own job got the same "not sure" reply.

A better way: accept an answer that fits the question, and ask only when it really does not.

EXTRA STEPSFamily game, turn 52. Also the gay and mixed couples.

The friend's job is asked twice

Earlier, Rafael described Camila's best friend as "Juliana, her college roommate... an ER nurse with big curly hair". When he added Juliana to the game, the wizard asked again what she does for work. Ryan and Andre got the same repeat for Priya and Jade.

A better way: fill in the job from the earlier answer, and let the buyer confirm it with one tap.

EXTRA STEPSFamily game, turns 49 to 54. Also the pet photos.

A photo upload gets no reply

After Rafael uploaded Mateo's photo, the chat went straight to the next question. There was no thank you, and no sign that the photo was good. The same thing happened for Luna and for the pet photos.

A better way: answer each photo with one short line, and say right away if no clear face was found.

SMALLERAll four games, 180 answers

Each answer takes about 8 seconds

We timed every answer the four buyers gave before Build It!. The middle wait was 11 seconds on our clock, and our clock adds about 3 seconds while it checks that the page is still. So a buyer waits about 8 seconds per question. The longest wait was 28 seconds.

A full interview is about 45 answers, so the buyer spends about 6 minutes just waiting.

A better way: show the next question while the warm reaction line is still being written.

answersthe middle wait17 seconds or more
SMALLERFamily game, turns 26 to 28

The look art does not follow later answers

Rafael picked a look for Camila that has a gold necklace, and the chat said "Ooh, that sparkly gold necklace". The very next question asked about her jewelry, and he said it is a thin silver necklace with an M and an L charm for the kids. The look was already locked in with gold.

A better way: ask about jewelry before the look is locked, or let a later answer update the picked look.

SMALLERAll four games, after Build It!

The build screen gives no time estimate

After Build It!, the screen says "Still weaving it all together, hang tight" above a bar, but it never says how long. "Your game is in!" took 4 to 9 minutes. The finished game then took more than an hour, because of the billing hold.

A better way: show a time range, such as "about 5 minutes", and say that it is fine to close the page.

SMALLERGay couple game, turn 32

A reaction garbled the inside joke

Ryan said that they both yell "Plot twist!" whenever plans go wrong, ever since the night they met at a bookstore. The reply turned it into yelling plot twist "when plans derail at the bookstore", as if the joke only happens there.

A better way: have the reaction reuse the buyer's own words, or keep it short.

WHERE TO START

Fix these five first, because a buyer would see them in the finished game or lose trust in the chat

Retry failed looksGive the partner and the kids a Try again button, and never build on a placeholder.
No dragon stand-insTheo and Mina became the house dragon in their games and on their boxes. Never publish a partner with stock art.
Unstick the family gameIt failed the template structure check twice. Its next try is at 9:16 PM.
Hide system textThe fingerprint and appearance messages must never show in the chat.
Speak to friends as friendsNo first dates, a Graduation button, and the buyer is never a friend extra.
